text:
jen: Heads-up — Customer ACME Corp reported a big increase in p99 for streaming responses today. Non-stream (sync) latency looks fine, but streaming TTFB p95/p99 jumped ~2x starting ~2024-09-10 14:00 UTC. They attached traces and a curl repro.
jen: Repro steps they gave:
```bash
curl -v -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' -H 'Accept: text/event-stream' \n  -d '{"model":"rwd/llama-small","prompt":"hello"}' \n  https://api.redwood.example/v1/stream/generate
```
jen: Customer says first chunk arrives ~300ms sometimes and then nothing for 1.2s before next chunk, total time OK but first-byte jitter is bad.
devon: Looking at traces — we see consistent gap between initial chunk and next token when request routed through our h2-edge in region eu-west-1. When routed through regional edge it’s normal.
alex: Can you paste the raw edge logs? I want to see flush events and socket write sizes.
jen: Pasting snippet from customer-proxy logs (sanitized):
```
[14:01:12.123] request-id=abcd flush-queued=true bytes-queued=72 last-flush=0
[14:01:12.426] request-id=abcd flush-sent=true bytes-flushed=72 latency-to-1st-chunk=303ms
[14:01:13.659] request-id=abcd next-chunk bytes=24
```
jen: So initial chunk shipped, then 1.2s gap to next chunk.
maria: Do we have any recent changes to the chunk coalescer / TCP_NODELAY or h2 windowing in edge? I remember a runtime tweak last week.
devon: We rolled an edge change that added an adaptive coalescing window for small writes to reduce tiny-packet overhead. That could explain added buffer delays for small token chunks. Config name: `edge.coalesce_small_writes_ms` — default bumped from 0 -> 50ms in canary.
alex: Ah, that matches. Customer language/SDK sometimes sends small 20-40B frames for punctuation tokens; adaptive coalescer was adding entropy.
jen: Customer is on Hosted prod via eu-west region, but if we force route to regional edge it looks fine.
samir: Is this impacting non-streaming? Probably not because sync aggregates before response. This is streaming only.
devon: Quick mitigations: 1) revert coalescing change on eu-west canary (fast rollback). 2) Add a per-route override: disable coalescing for /v1/stream/* endpoints. 3) Short-term customer workaround: set `Accept: text/event-stream` + `Prefer: chunked=1` (we can treat as a hint).
maria: I suggest we also add a heuristic to flush first chunk immediately (force-flush-first=true) so TTFB stays low even if coalescing is enabled for later chunks.
jen: I created INC-2024-447 with customer ticket number. Assigning to devon+alex for triage.
deploy-bot: Started rollback job rollback-edge-eu-west-1747. Job id: rb-174650.
deploy-bot: Rollback succeeded on 3/3 canaries at 14:22 UTC.
devon: After rollback, we re-ran customer repro — TTFB p99 dropped back to baseline (~120ms). Re-run logs:
```
[14:24:02.010] request-id=abcd flush-sent=true bytes-flushed=72 latency-to-1st-chunk=118ms
[14:24:02.142] next-chunk bytes=34
```
devon: That confirms coalescer is the primary vector. We'll push a per-route disable behind a feature flag and schedule a safe rollout with metrics gating.
alex: Long-term we should: 1) expose `force-flush-first` at runtime for streaming endpoints, 2) add telemetry: count of flush delays > 200ms for streaming.3) Update the canary checklist so coalescer changes require streaming-coldstart smoke tests.
maria: For customer communication: Jen, please send a short note: we identified edge coalescing as root cause, rolled back a canary, and will enable a route-level fix. Offer to route ACME to regional edge as a temporary option.
samir: Also verify whether TLS session resumption interplay with h2 windowing could amplify gaps — add to postmortem.
jen: Drafted customer reply and sent — they confirmed improvement after redirect. They've asked for a permanent mitigation.
devon: Action items (short):
- devon: add per-route coalescer override + feature flag (ETA 1d)
- alex: add telemetry for first-chunk delta >200ms + alert (ETA 2d)
- maria: update rollout playbook and add streaming smoke test (ETA 3d)
- jen: customer comms and follow-up
jen: Will keep thread updated. If anyone wants logs/traces I uploaded full HAR to the incident ticket.
maria: Also, small note — some clients (mobile SDK) open long-lived HTTP/1.1 connections which saw less regression. Must add that to hypothesis list for root cause doc.
alex: I'll own the incident postmortem and link to the PRs + rollout notes.
jen: Thanks everyone — closing the immediate escalation. Will reopen if customer sees a regression. :thumbsup:
